title.en: Frontier layer invariants of a breadth-first traversal

summary: Check that dequeued distances are non-decreasing, vertices are enqueued once and predecessor chains match reported distances.
objective: The traversal log satisfies the layer invariants for reachable vertices, and every reachable predecessor chain length equals the reported distance.
applies_when: A traversal is animated over a graph with a visible frontier.
Distances or layers are reported to the viewer.
The layout suggests spatial distances that are not the graph metric.
intent_signals: check the distances in this traversal
example_prompts: Check the frontier invariants of this breadth-first search scene.

principles: Breadth-first order is an invariant of the queue rather than of the drawing: dequeued distances are non-decreasing and consecutive values differ by at most one.
Discovery marks on enqueue, not on dequeue; marking late is the classic defect that enqueues a vertex twice and inflates the frontier.
Distance here is edge count, so the geometric length of a drawn edge must never influence the traversal or the reported distance.
implementation: Instrument the traversal to log every enqueue and dequeue with the vertex, its assigned distance and the current queue contents.
After the run verify that dequeued distances are non-decreasing and that consecutive values differ by zero or one.
Reconstruct the predecessor chain of every reachable vertex back to the source and compare its length with the reported distance, listing unreachable vertices separately.
Include a disconnected component and a graph with several equally short paths, then re-run with a different neighbour order.
observable_checks: Each vertex reachable from the source is enqueued exactly once, no vertex is enqueued after being dequeued, and unreachable vertices are never enqueued at all.
Dequeued distances never decrease and never jump by more than one; a larger jump identifies a queue being used as a stack.

Every reachable vertex has a predecessor chain to the source whose length equals its reported distance; unreachable vertices have no chain and no finite distance, and a different neighbour order changes only which equally short tree appears.

known_limits: Applies to unweighted traversal; it says nothing about weighted cost, optimality under weights, or running time.
Authored verification guidance; no traversal was executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: Breadth-first search maintains a queue of vertices that have been marked but whose adjacency lists have not been checked, and for any vertex reachable from the source it computes a path with the fewest edges.
claims.scope: Unweighted graphs; fewest edges rather than weighted cost or drawn length.

source_refs.locator: Breadth-first search: queue of marked vertices and the shortest-path property
